audits.title: FP4.6 - A Re-audit on the completion of pathology request forms following Colorectal Cancer Resection
audits.standard: Royal College of Pathologists parameters for colorectal cancer resection request forms

cycle2.result: Approach 30%; diagrams 36%; preoperative therapy 20%; no significant overall improvement.

audits.other_findings: Consultants who emphasised form completion achieved 97% type of surgery and 91% diagrams; marginal improvement in screening, familial cancer and IBD information.
audits.citation: Umenze F, Saraee D, Khadka S, Coup A, Kaur G. FP4.6 - A Re-audit on the completion of pathology request forms following Colorectal Cancer Resection. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.375.

audits.title: Improving the interaction between the ophthalmology and histopathology departments.
audits.setting: Ophthalmology department, Royal Hallamshire Hospital, Sheffield

cycle1.result: Request form completion reviewed (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Redesigned ophthalmic histopathology request form circulated.

cycle2.result: Improved completion of important sections of the form.

audits.title: Unveiling documentation deficiencies: a clinical audit of histopathology request forms at a tertiary care hospital.

cycle1.result: High compliance for patient profile details but patient contact information recorded in only 39.7%; clinical notes incomplete in 27.3%.

audits.intervention: Educational intervention based on initial findings.

cycle2.result: Improved documentation of patient contact details and biopsy nature (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Hospital admission and biopsy details were well documented at baseline.
audits.citation: Tariq MD, Hamza HM, Ahsan A, Sarfraz T, Malik MM, Aneeqa S, et al.. Unveiling documentation deficiencies: a clinical audit of histopathology request forms at a tertiary care hospital. Ann Med Surg (Lond). 2025;87(4):2000-2005. doi:10.1097/ms9.0000000000003038. PMID: 40212126.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Intervention to Enhance Documentation on Histopathology Request Forms.
audits.standard: Completeness of histopathology request form documentation (standard not named in abstract)

cycle1.result: Clinical history 0%; presenting complaints 3.2%; examination findings 73.6%; radiological findings 44.4%; laboratory results 41.2%; drug history 6%; biopsy time 3.2%; provisional diagnosis 49.2%.

audits.intervention: Standardised request form, clinician engagement and improved access to forms (PDSA).

cycle2.result: Clinical history 62%; presenting complaints 73%; examination findings 96%; radiological findings 95%; laboratory results 81%; drug history 48%; biopsy time 66%; provisional diagnosis 78%.

audits.other_findings: Drug history remained under 50% after the intervention.
audits.citation: Ansar F, Rauf MS, Kinwan Khan M, Rauf U, Ahmad MB, Ishtiaq A, et al.. A Quality Improvement Intervention to Enhance Documentation on Histopathology Request Forms. Cureus. 2025;17(3):e81317. doi:10.7759/cureus.81317. PMID: 40291197.

audits.title: Are We Providing Enough Information to the Pathologists? An Audit of Filling of Histopathology Request Forms for Surgically Resected Tumours.
audits.standard: Adequacy of clinical and demographic information on histopathology request forms
audits.setting: Department of Pathology, Dow University of Health Sciences, Karachi

cycle1.result: Patient name 99.4% (174); medical record number 64.6% (113); doctor's phone number 19.4% (34); clinical diagnosis 93.7% (164); correct nature of biopsy 38.3% (67)

audits.other_findings: Operative details given in half of forms; symptom duration 57.1% (100). Specialty is pathology.
audits.citation: Siddiqui MS, Kumar S, Kumar D, Khalid S, Hassan W, Khatri M. Are We Providing Enough Information to the Pathologists? An Audit of Filling of Histopathology Request Forms for Surgically Resected Tumours. J Coll Physicians Surg Pak. 2024;34(4):484-488. doi:10.29271/jcpsp.2024.04.484. PMID: 38576295.
